139154.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This PR is the third step of splitting the work originally proposed in #138883.

It deprecates the old watch-cache-specific LIST metrics:

- `apiserver_cache_list_total`
- `apiserver_cache_list_fetched_objects_total`
- `apiserver_cache_list_returned_objects_total`

These metrics are now superseded by the unified
`apiserver_storage_list_*` metric family introduced in the earlier stages.

The watch cache path already records the unified storage metrics with
`storage="watchcache"`, so the old cache-specific metric family is no longer the
canonical way to observe LIST requests served from watch cache.



#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

fixes: #138264  
Original work: #138883  
Stage 1: #139082  
Stage 2: #139125

#### Special notes for your reviewer:


Stage breakdown:

- stage 1: move the existing `apiserver_storage_list_*` metrics into the shared `pkg/storage/metrics` package
  - #139082
- stage 2: add the labels needed for the unified storage metrics (`storage` and `index`)
  - #139125
- stage 3: deprecate the old cache-specific metrics
  - #139154


for ALPHA metrics, setting `DeprecatedVersion` causes the metric to stop being
exposed by default in the current development version.

With the earlier stages already merged, the watch cache path is covered by the
unified metrics instead:

- `apiserver_storage_list_total{storage="watchcache"}`
- `apiserver_storage_list_fetched_objects_total{storage="watchcache"}`
- `apiserver_storage_list_returned_objects_total{storage="watchcache"}`


#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
The deprecated ALPHA metrics `apiserver_cache_list_total`, `apiserver_cache_list_fetched_objects_total`, and `apiserver_cache_list_returned_objects_total` are no longer exposed by default.  
Should migrate to the unified `apiserver_storage_list_*` metrics with `storage="watchcache"` label.
```

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:
/kind api-change
/kind deprecation

-->
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

A pod can become stuck in unschedulable queue in the following sequence:

1. While the preemptor pod is waiting for preemption, change the cluster in a way that will re-queue the pod. The DefaultPreemption's PreEnqueue will return Unschedulable which will gate the pod
2. The relevant plugins don't return fwk.Queue hint once the victim pods are deleted. This can happen if there's a bug in queue hint implementation (e.g. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139161)

A gated pod will not react to flushes, meaning it fully relies on the plugin's queue hints to activate. Since the plugin hasn't returned the expected queue hint, the pod is stuck in unschedulable queue forever.

The fix is to make gated pods react to flushes, providing a failsafe. Alternatively, we could ungate the preemptor pod once the preemption completes.

139168.author: liggitt
139168.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/kind regression

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/139132

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

This changes the cri-api value field from `string` to `bytes`. This encodes identically on the wire, but removes the requirement that the value be valid utf-8. 139287.text: Fixed a regression in 1.36 where modifications to scheduling directives (nodeSelector, tolerations, node affinity) on suspended Jobs were rejected if the JobSuspended condition had not yet been set by the job controller.
139287.markdown: Fixed a regression in 1.36 where modifications to scheduling directives (nodeSelector, tolerations, node affinity) on suspended Jobs were rejected if the JobSuspended condition had not yet been set by the job controller. ([#139287](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139287), [@kannon92](https://github.com/kannon92)) [SIG Apps and Testing]
139287.author: kannon92
139287.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/kind regression

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When the `MutableSchedulingDirectivesForSuspendedJobs` feature gate is enabled (Beta in 1.36), modifications to scheduling directives on a suspended Job are rejected if the `JobSuspended=True` condition hasn't been set yet by the job controller. This breaks external controllers like MultiKueue that inject scheduling directives immediately after creating a suspended Job.

The fix preserves the `notStarted` path as an OR condition alongside the `JobSuspended` condition check, so that suspended Jobs that have never started can still have their scheduling directives mutated — matching pre-1.36 behavior.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #139281

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The one-line fix is in `pkg/registry/batch/job/strategy.go`. The condition changes from:

```go
suspended && batchvalidation.IsConditionTrue(oldJob.Status.Conditions, batch.JobSuspended) && oldJob.Status.Active == 0
```

to:

```go
suspended && (notStarted || (batchvalidation.IsConditionTrue(oldJob.Status.Conditions, batch.JobSuspended) && oldJob.Status.Active == 0))
```

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed a regression in 1.36 where modifications to scheduling directives (nodeSelector, tolerations, node affinity) on suspended Jobs were rejected if the JobSuspended condition had not yet been set by the job controller.
```


#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When scheduling PodGroups, the DRA scheduler plugin tracks pending allocations shared between Pods in a PodGroup with reference counting. The Reserve phase increments the count, but both the PreBind and Unreserve phases were decrementing the count when PreBind failed. This PR removes the decrement from PreBind after it fails, relying on the existing decrement in Unreserve. More details in the commit message.

139516.text: kube-proxy now truncates nftables comments to the kernel's 128-byte limit before programming service maps, avoiding sync failures for long Service names.
139516.markdown: Kube-proxy now truncates nftables comments to the kernel's 128-byte limit before programming service maps, avoiding sync failures for long Service names. ([#139516](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139516), [@Vinayak9769](https://github.com/Vinayak9769)) [SIG Network]
139516.author: Vinayak9769
139516.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
Truncates nftables element comments in kube-proxy to the maximum length accepted by the kernel before programming service maps. This prevents nftables sync failures when Service names are long enough to exceed the 128-byte comment limit.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Fixes #139515

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
The change only affects cosmetic nftables comments. The truncation is applied once in `syncProxyRules`, which covers all service map entries that reuse `svcInfo.nameString`. Happy to make any other changes if needed :)

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
kube-proxy now truncates nftables comments to the kernel's 128-byte limit before programming service maps, avoiding sync failures for long Service names.
```

N/A
